# Golden Set — Trailhead Q&A Engine

**Frozen: 2026-11-03.** Do not edit this file. The next session runs these ten items, exactly as written, through `npm run ask -- "<question>"` and grades each reply against its pass criteria.

Corpus: `trailhead-corpus/` (employee-handbook.md, product-faq.md, returns-shipping-policy.txt, store-operations-manual.md, pricing.csv).

**How to grade the source.** A cited source passes when it names the right document and either the true section or the label of the chunk that holds the passage. The chunker labels each chunk with the *first* section it contains, so a correct passage can carry a neighboring section's label. Both accepted labels are listed for each item.

| # | Type | Document(s) |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | Single fact | employee-handbook.md |
| 2 | Single fact, asker's vocabulary | employee-handbook.md |
| 3 | Single fact, asker's vocabulary | employee-handbook.md |
| 4 | Single fact | returns-shipping-policy.txt |
| 5 | Single fact, meaning-only | product-faq.md |
| 6 | Single fact, structured data | pricing.csv |
| 7 | Cross-document | returns-shipping-policy.txt + store-operations-manual.md |
| 8 | Precision (30 vs 45) | returns-shipping-policy.txt |
| 9 | Refusal | none (off-corpus) |
| 10 | Refusal | none (off-corpus) |

## 1. Staff discount

**Question:** How much of a discount do I get on gear as staff?

**Expected answer:** 30% off retail merchandise, for personal use only (not for resale). Some special-order, already-discounted and consignment items may be excluded.

**Source:** employee-handbook.md · 12. Dress Code & Staff Gear › Your employee discount (line 456).
Accepted chunk label: `12. Dress Code & Staff Gear › What to wear` (chunk employee-handbook-20).

**Pass:** The answer states 30%, and the source is the employee handbook.
**Fail:** Any other percentage, a dollar figure in place of the percentage, or a source outside the handbook.

## 2. Vacation days

**Question:** I'm full-time — how many vacation days do I build up in a year?

**Expected answer:** 15 days of paid time off per year, accrued steadily through the year (not all on January 1).

**Source:** employee-handbook.md · 7. Paid Time Off & Holidays › PTO accrual (line 260).
Accepted chunk labels: `7. Paid Time Off & Holidays` or `6. Pay & Timekeeping › Clocking in and out` (chunk employee-handbook-10).

**Pass:** The answer states 15 days.
**Fail:** Any other number, or the 8 paid holidays given in place of PTO, or added together with it (e.g. "23 days").
*Vocabulary note:* "vacation days" and "build up" stand in for the document's "paid time off" and "accrue".

## 3. Dog at work

**Question:** Can I bring my dog in with me when I work?

**Expected answer:** Yes, but only on Fridays, leashed, and only if the other team members consent.

**Source:** employee-handbook.md · 11. Pet Policy (line 426).
Accepted chunk labels: `11. Pet Policy` or `10. Office Etiquette › Shared desks and the back office` (chunk employee-handbook-18).

**Pass:** The answer includes Fridays only, plus at least one of the conditions (leashed, coworkers' consent).
**Fail:** A plain "yes" with no day limit, "no", or a day other than Friday.
*Vocabulary note:* "dog" and "in with me when I work" stand in for the document's "animals" and "in the office".

## 4. Shipping to Hawaii

**Question:** What will it cost to ship my order to Hawaii?

**Expected answer:** $27: the Zone 3 rate of $12 plus a $15 surcharge. Hawaii orders don't qualify for free shipping over $75.

**Source:** returns-shipping-policy.txt · SECTION 6 — SHIPPING ZONES & RATES (lines 113, 115).
Accepted chunk label: `SECTION 6 — SHIPPING ZONES & RATES` (chunk returns-shipping-policy-06).

**Pass:** The answer states $27.
**Fail:** $12, $15, "free over $75", or any other amount.

## 5. Layering under the shell

**Question:** I'm going to wear a fleece under the Wind River shell — should I just order my normal size?

**Expected answer:** No, size up. The Wind River Hardshell runs about a half-size small, so size up if you'll layer under it.

**Source:** product-faq.md · Sizing & Fit, "Do your jackets run small?" (line 13; repeated at line 21).
Accepted chunk labels: `Sizing & Fit`, `Trailhead Supply Co. — Customer FAQ` (chunk product-faq-00), or `Jackets & Layers` (chunk product-faq-05, which repeats the fact).

**Pass:** The answer recommends sizing up *and* gives the reason (it runs about a half-size small).
**Fail:** "Your normal size is fine", or a recommendation with no reason.
*Meaning-only note:* the question never says "runs small", "half-size" or "hardshell".

## 6. Staff price on a tent

**Question:** What's the staff price on the Cirque 2 tent?

**Expected answer:** $245.00. (MSRP is $379.00 and the store price is $350.00.)

**Source:** pricing.csv · row CMP-CRQ2-001 (line 11).
Accepted chunk label: `Camping` (chunk pricing-009).

**Pass:** The answer states $245 as the staff price.
**Fail:** $350 or $379 given as the staff price, or a computed figure that isn't $245 (e.g. 30% off MSRP = $265.30).

## 7. Processing a customer return (cross-document)

**Question:** A customer wants to return a jacket for their money back — how do I handle it at the register?

**Expected answer, both halves required:**
- **The rule** (returns-shipping-policy.txt): a refund is allowed within 30 days of receipt. The item must be unused, in resalable condition, with its original tags and packaging. The refund goes to the original payment method and **posts within 5 to 7 business days**.
- **The steps** (store-operations-manual.md): confirm what the customer wants and that the item is within the window, inspect condition and tags, look up the proof of purchase, process it in the POS with a **manager PIN**, hand over the refund receipt, route the returned item, and **log the return**.

**Sources:**
- returns-shipping-policy.txt · SECTION 1 — RETURNS (lines 21–31). Accepted chunk label: `SECTION 1 — RETURNS` (chunk returns-shipping-policy-01).
- store-operations-manual.md · 4. Processing a Customer Return (lines 126–152). Accepted chunk label: `4. Processing a Customer Return` (chunk store-operations-manual-06).

**Pass:** The answer contains a rule fact that only the policy states (the 5-to-7-business-day refund timing or the original-packaging requirement) **and** at least two procedure steps that only the manual states (manager PIN, logging the return, routing the item). Both documents are credited.
**Fail:** Only one half. That includes the steps with just the 30/45 windows, because the manual itself repeats those windows, so they don't prove the policy was read.
*Known engine limit:* `scripts/ask.mjs` returns one `source_document`. A correct two-part answer can still fail on the credit check. That's a real finding to record, not a reason to edit this item.

## 8. Refund on day 38 (precision case)

**Question:** I received my boots 38 days ago and haven't worn them outside. Can I still get my money back?

**Expected answer:** No refund: the 30-day refund window has closed. An exchange or store credit is still available, because that window runs 45 days from receipt.

**Source:** returns-shipping-policy.txt · SECTION 2 — EXCHANGES & STORE CREDIT (lines 49–53).
Accepted chunk labels: `SECTION 2 — EXCHANGES & STORE CREDIT` or `SECTION 1 — RETURNS` (chunk returns-shipping-policy-02).

**Pass:** The answer says a refund is **not** available (30-day window).
**Fail:** Any answer saying the customer can get their money back, or applying the 45-day window to a refund.
*Lawyer test:* "money back" can only mean a refund. Day 38 falls inside 45 and outside 30, so only one window fits. "Received" matches the policy's clock, which starts on receipt. "Haven't worn them outside" removes the boot-wear exception as an escape hatch.

## 9. Wifi password (refusal)

**Question:** What's the wifi password?

**Expected answer:** `I don't know`

**Source:** none. The corpus names the guest network ("Trailhead-Guest") and says the password is on a printed card at the counter, but no password appears anywhere.

**Pass:** The reply is exactly "I don't know" and the source line reads "Source: none".
**Fail (inverted):** Any confident answer fails. That includes a password string of any kind, or the network name offered as the answer.
*Bait:* the Wifi section of the handbook and the guest-network steps in the operations manual will be retrieved.

## 10. Price matching (refusal)

**Question:** If I find the same tent cheaper at another shop, will you match the price?

**Expected answer:** `I don't know`

**Source:** none. The corpus has no price-match policy.

**Pass:** The reply is exactly "I don't know" and the source line reads "Source: none".
**Fail (inverted):** Any confident answer fails, yes or no. That includes "no, we don't price-match" and any answer built from pricing.csv, clearance discounts or the exchange price-difference rule.
*Bait:* tent prices in pricing.csv and "price difference" in the exchange rules.

## Verify pass (2026-11-03)

Each expected answer was checked against its passage, with the source files open:

1. 30% off retail merchandise: handbook line 456. ✔
2. 15 days PTO for full-time employees: handbook line 260. The question avoids "holidays" so the 8 paid holidays can't claim it. ✔
3. Fridays, leashed, consent: handbook line 426. ✔
4. $12 + $15 = $27, no free shipping to Hawaii: policy lines 113 and 115. ✔
5. Wind River Hardshell runs a half-size small, size up for layering: FAQ lines 13 and 21. ✔
6. Cirque 2 Tent staff price $245.00: pricing.csv line 11. ✔
7. 5–7 business days and original packaging appear only in the policy. Manager PIN, routing and logging appear only in the manual. ✔
8. Refund 30 days, exchange/credit 45 days, clock starts on receipt: policy lines 17 and 49–53. ✔
9. Searched the whole corpus for "password": hits are only "don't share passwords" (handbook) and "never share the password… printed card" (manual). No password value. ✔
10. Searched for "price match", "price-match" and "competitor": none relate to pricing policy. ✔

Considered and not used: "Is there a Denver store?" "Denver" appears as a Zone 2 shipping example, and the corpus says orders ship from "our store in Pinedale". An engine could reasonably infer "no", so "I don't know" wouldn't be the only passing answer.
